page.pageTitle: Free wedding photo video maker – slideshow for Instagram Reels
page.pageDescription: Turn your wedding photos into a free video: add 3 to 60 photos, pick 9:16 for Reels and TikTok or 16:9 for YouTube, and download an MP4. Nothing is uploaded.
page.homeLink: Make a free video from your wedding photos
page.heroTitle: A video from your wedding photos in minutes
page.heroLead: Add your wedding photos, choose the shape and length, and download a finished MP4. The camera slowly drifts in and out on each photo, and one photo fades gently into the next. No sign-up, no watermark and nothing to install.
page.privacyBadge: Your photos stay on your device – nothing is uploaded.

how.title: Add your photos
how.body: Choose 3 to 60 photos from your phone or computer. The page checks them and gets them ready – it takes a few seconds per photo.

how.title: Choose the shape, length and pace
how.body: Portrait 9:16 for Instagram Reels, Stories and TikTok, or landscape 16:9 for YouTube and websites. The length adapts to how many photos you have, and the pace can be calm or lively.

how.title: Watch the preview and download the MP4
how.body: The preview shows exactly what will be in the video. One tap turns it into an MP4 file you can share straight away.

features: Every photo you add is always in it – none get left out.
Photos play in the order they were taken, or by file name.
Anything from a few seconds to three minutes, depending on how many photos you have.
A calm pace for the ceremony and portraits, a lively one for the party and quick highlights.
Slow camera movement and soft fades, just like in a wedding film.
It points out any photo that might spoil the video, so you can leave it out.
The video has no sound – add music right in Instagram or TikTok, where it's licensed for you to use.
page.privacyBody: Everything happens right in your browser: checking the photos, the preview and making the video. Nothing is uploaded to any server and we keep nothing – when you close the page, your photos go with it. Hidden details, such as where a photo was taken, are also removed while it's being prepared.
limits: 3 to 60 photos in JPEG, PNG or WebP. (iPhone photos in HEIC format: save them as JPEG first, or send them to yourself via AirDrop or email.)
Each photo at least 1000 px on its shorter side, and no more than 62 megapixels or 40 MB.
Works best in an up-to-date Chrome, Edge or Safari. It's quicker on a computer than on a phone.
Making the video takes about as long as the video itself – keep the page open until it's done.
page.weddingBody: This tool was made for couples photographed by Pavel Prokeš, a wedding photographer from Prague. Every couple he works with gets a short video for social media, in both portrait and landscape, ready and waiting in their online gallery – together with all their photos to download and the photos their guests took on the day.

faq.a: Yes. No sign-up, no watermark and no limit on how many videos you make. The tool is run by wedding photographer Pavel Prokeš as a gift to couples and their guests.
No. Your photos are processed only in your browser and are never sent to a server. Close the page and nothing is left behind.
Music in the video could run into copyright problems on Instagram, TikTok or YouTube. Add it in the app instead, where it's licensed for you to use.

faq.q: How many photos can I use, and how long will the video be?
faq.a: 3 to 60 photos. Every one of them is always in the video, so the length depends on how many there are and the pace you choose – the page only offers lengths that make sense.

faq.q: Why won't it work on my phone?
faq.a: Making the video needs a recent browser and plenty of memory. Try an up-to-date Chrome or Safari, fewer photos, or a computer.
9:16 portrait for Instagram Reels, Stories and TikTok; 16:9 landscape for YouTube, a website or showing on a screen at the wedding.
